# isEmail

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is an email address.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isEmail() — Checks whether a value is an email address. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isEmail(email: unknown): email is string;
```

The address is split at a single `@`: the domain is checked the way `isValidDomain` checks one, and the local part must be non-empty and free of spaces. It is a format check, not proof that the mailbox exists.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description                                     |
| :-------- | :-------- | :---------------------------------------------- |
| `email`   | `unknown` | The value to check, which could be of any type. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is an email address; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `email` to `string` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isEmail("user@example.com"); // => true
isEmail("first.last@sub.example.co.uk"); // => true
isEmail("user@@example.com"); // => false
isEmail("user@"); // => false
isEmail("example.com"); // => false
isEmail(""); // => false
```
